title: Workflow Composer Checkpoint D invalid-edit recovery
summary: The local engineer edited and moved the review block, contained an output-to-output connection without changing the last-valid draft or saved revision, applied the named correction, validated, and saved revision 2 with no browser diagnostics.

manualSteps.label: Create composition
manualSteps.instruction: Open **Workflow Composer**, click **Create working draft**, then add **Capture input**, **Engineering work**, **Review**, and **Release boundary**.

manualSteps.label: Edit review block
manualSteps.instruction: Select **Review product definition**, change its definition and position, then apply both edits.

manualSteps.label: Attempt invalid connection
manualSteps.instruction: Delete **connection.definition-to-review**, choose **Product definition · output** as source and **Accepted definition · output** as target, then click **Create connection**.

manualSteps.label: Correct connection
manualSteps.instruction: Keep the source, choose **Product definition · input** as target, then click **Create connection**.

steps.label: Create a separate working draft
steps.summary: Revision 1 opened under explicit provisional authority.
steps.purpose: Begin from an isolated empty working draft.
steps.expected: An empty revision 1 opens with no released or executable authority.
steps.actual: Revision 1 opened with Working draft and Not released · Not executable labels.

steps.label: Add Capture input
steps.summary: Capture input was added through the bounded palette.
steps.purpose: Build the representative valid starting graph.
steps.expected: The next complete valid candidate replaces the working copy.
steps.actual: The block and its reciprocal declarations appeared without browser diagnostics.

steps.label: Add Engineering work
steps.summary: Engineering work was added through the bounded palette.
steps.purpose: Build the representative valid starting graph.
steps.expected: The next complete valid candidate replaces the working copy.
steps.actual: The block and its reciprocal declarations appeared without browser diagnostics.

steps.label: Add Review
steps.summary: Review was added through the bounded palette.
steps.purpose: Build the representative valid starting graph.
steps.expected: The next complete valid candidate replaces the working copy.
steps.actual: The block and its reciprocal declarations appeared without browser diagnostics.

steps.label: Add Release boundary
steps.summary: Release boundary was added through the bounded palette.
steps.purpose: Build the representative valid starting graph.
steps.expected: The next complete valid candidate replaces the working copy.
steps.actual: The block and its reciprocal declarations appeared without browser diagnostics.

steps.label: Edit and move the review block
steps.summary: The selected block changed definition and layout without changing unrelated identities.
steps.purpose: Demonstrate direct routine editing before invalid recovery.
steps.action: Changed the selected block title, purpose, X, and Y, then applied both edits.
steps.expected: Canvas, text, and inspector agree on the same stable block identity and new values.
steps.actual: All three surfaces show the edited block at layout 720,96; revision remains 1.

steps.label: Remove one valid connection
steps.summary: The selected relationship was removed as one valid working-copy transaction.
steps.purpose: Create a valid opening for the corrected relationship.
steps.expected: Only that connection disappears; ports and saved revision remain unchanged.
steps.actual: The relationship count fell from three to two and revision remained 1.

steps.label: Contain an output-to-output connection
steps.summary: The invalid candidate was isolated with specific affected identities and correction; the two-connection last-valid draft and revision 1 remained unchanged.
steps.purpose: Prove invalid intent cannot corrupt working or saved state.
steps.action: Selected Product definition output as source, Accepted definition output as target, and clicked Create connection.
steps.expected: The invalid connection is rejected, affected identities are marked, and a bounded correction is shown.
steps.actual: CONNECTION_TARGET_INVALID identified the output target, stated it is not an input, and directed the engineer to choose an existing input; no candidate connection appeared.

steps.label: Apply the named connection correction
steps.summary: Choosing the compatible input cleared the diagnostic and restored a valid three-connection graph.
steps.purpose: Prove recovery preserves the earlier edit and produces a saveable candidate.
steps.action: Changed only the target to Product definition input and clicked Create connection.
steps.expected: The correction clears the diagnostic and appears in both diagram and text.
steps.actual: The diagnostic cleared; the corrected connection appears in diagram and text while the review edit and position remain.

steps.label: Validate the recovered draft
steps.summary: Server validation accepted the corrected candidate.
steps.purpose: Verify the complete recovered graph before persistence.
steps.expected: Validation passes with no contradictory local or server diagnostic.
steps.actual: The status and inspector both report validation passed.

steps.label: Save only the corrected draft
steps.summary: The valid recovered candidate advanced atomically to revision 2.
steps.purpose: Complete Checkpoint D without persisting the rejected candidate.
steps.action: Clicked Save draft after validation passed.
steps.expected: Only the corrected candidate advances to revision 2.
steps.actual: Revision 2 saved with the edited review block and compatible connection; the rejected output-to-output relationship is absent.
